Step 6c is complete. Report at `research/frontier-15-alpha-6c.md`.

## What I audited

I computed every edge out of all 392 in-flight items from disk — 1,409 in total — resolving targets through the library page files rather than `plan-spec.json`, because the spec's item lists don't cover the legacy foundational pages and resolving against it first made 26 live published targets read as unresolved.

| class | edges |
|---|---|
| same page | 528 |
| same batch, A→B | 141 |
| **cross-batch in-run** | **0** |
| **cross-level, into published** | **740** |

Zero undeclared page edges, zero plan-order violations, zero `ai-generated` statements used as dependency targets, zero forward references, zero unresolved targets.

**Cross-batch zero is forced, not a lapse** — no A page in the run declares another run A page in its `requires`, so a cross-batch citation would be an undeclared-prerequisite error. I checked the live alternative (duplication) instead: highest cross-batch statement overlap across ~66,000 comparisons is 0.219, shared vocabulary rather than shared mathematics. Both named seams check out: the Sylow index-*p* item is cited by nothing in-run and *is* stated in existence form; batch 3's closure machinery is unreached.

## Six defects, all repaired

I read all 448 cross-level theorem/lemma/proposition/corollary citations against their sources, and screened the 292 definition citations for added inferential clauses (22 candidates, all read, all clean).

One **fatal**: `cor-classification-of-groups-of-order-one-hundred-five` [L11] ends mid-clause at *"and the resulting map."* — the biconditional has no consequent, so step 3.1's `G ≅ C₅ × H` had no support at all. Five **nonfatal** inflations/omissions: an unlicensed `≤ H` on the coset-action kernel, "and therefore algebraic" on a finiteness theorem, a natural-transformation criterion attributed to a proposition that doesn't state it, a dropped "Assume the Axiom of Choice", and a puncture generalised from the origin.

In every case the item's mathematics was sound and the defect lived only in the reader-facing Facts line — and in two cases the *contract's* recorded quote was already correct. **No gate compares those two strings**: `citation-fidelity` checks quote-vs-source, `truncated-citation` checks factline-vs-source, neither checks factline-vs-quote. That gap is recorded in all six ledger rows.

## Receipts and gates

All nine dispatch gates green, plus five confirmation gates. Two honest notes: `finite-smoke` runs 4 checks over 4 of 324 items (known vacuity, already routed earlier — I didn't reopen it), and `gate-liveness` exits 1 bare because it skips `coverage-checklist` without explicit `--checklists`.

**Spine receipt** — I read all 58 proofs, not just attested them; every note names that proof's actual route. Nothing in the spine is wrong. **Impact receipt** — 392 interfaces, 347 dispositions, each naming the actual interfaces consumed and attributing the semantic reading of in-batch edges to 6a/6b rather than claiming I re-read 347 proofs.

## One thing for you

**90 of 392 items end their Statement with a bare "See [[some-id]]" pointer; the published corpus does this in 9 of 4,935.** Not a correctness defect — `depcheck` shows every pointer is properly declared — but it's a visible voice shift across 90 pages' worth of statements, applied by more than one Beta. Fixing it now costs 90 edits; after step 7 freezes it costs 90 edits plus 90 rejudges. I deliberately filed no ledger row, since it fits none of the four defect classes and would corrupt the accuracy statistic.

I left the working tree uncommitted. My six repaired items, four batch contracts, two receipts, ledger rows and report sit alongside earlier stages' uncommitted work (`ARCHITECTURE.md`, `QUALITY-CONTROLS.md`, three new tools, the audit dispatch tree), and I didn't want to bundle another agent's work under a 6c message. Say the word and I'll commit just mine.

Nothing at 6c blocks step 7.
